children: By Keshav SinghChundawat

Australian shares slid on Monday, dragged by miners, outweighing gains in financials as investors digested Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks signalling the possibility of a U.S. rate hike if inflation persists.
The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index
fell 0.2% to 9,076.00 points. It rose 1.1% in August, surpassing an average 0.1% growth in the same month over the past decade.
U.S. Fed Chair Warsh said on Friday the U.S. central bank will "have work to do" if policymakers don't get the confidence they need that inflation is returning to the 2% target.
"Warsh’s signal that the Fed is prepared to hike if inflation remains sticky raises the bar globally," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

In Australia, swaps imply a more than 50% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in September, compared with 16% prior to July inflation data released last week that showed prices rose more than expected.

"If the world’s major central banks are still leaning toward tighter policy, it clears the way for the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) to maintain its willingness to raise rates should the inflation and economic data warrant it," Waterer said.
In Sydney, miners
lost 2.1% in their worst session since August 14 on softer copper prices. BHP
and Rio  Tinto
shed 1.8% and 1.6%, respectively. However, the sub-index jumped 12.7% this month, its biggest monthly gain since November 2022.
The gold sub-index
dropped 4.3% in the session.
Financials
advanced 1.1% in their best day in nearly a month, with the "Big Four" banks climbing between 0.9% and 1.9%.
Meanwhile, Cochlear
and Sonic Healthcare
tumbled 1.6% and 2.3%, respectively, as MSCI removed the stocks from the Australia index, effective trading close on Monday.
In New Zealand, the S&P/NZX 50 index
rose 1.1% to 13,917.30 points, marking its best day since mid-June. The index advanced 1.6% in August, its fourth straight month of gains.
The Reserve Bank of New Zealand is widely expected to hike interest rates by 25 basis points to 2.75% at its meeting on Wednesday, a Reuters poll showed.
